Kleszczele Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kleszczele, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Kleszczele from the 16th century, though settlement was banned from 1688; the community only developed after Poland's partitions, reaching 645 (31%) by 1931, mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, established in the 19th century, received the bodies of six Jews shot by the Gestapo on November 5, 1942. A 1986 government survey warned of the site's 'complete obliteration'; a 1996 fire further damaged the grounds. A 1993 monument commemorates murdered local Jews, with a second plaque honoring five named ghetto survivors: Josef Białostocki, Izak Kleszczelski, Zelman Waserman, Symche Bursztyn, and Lejzer Melamed.
